transcript:
Header: 2026-09-29 07:32 UTC — Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Anya Li (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (NovaPay Head of ML), Evan Zhou (NovaPay Infra), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Sanjay Rao (SRE)

Summary: quick sync on POC throughput numbers, tuning continuous batching and concurrency targets, addressing observed queueing spikes, agreement to run an extended load test and share configs + benchmark sheet.

Topics:
- Current throughput & latency observed (baseline vs tuned)
- Continuous batching parameters (batch max_tokens, batch_window_ms)
- Concurrency targets per model shard and autoscale triggers
- Queueing/backpressure behavior and retry policies
- Next tests, artifacts to share

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, um we did a quick agenda — review the last week's numbers, go over tuning, then action items. carlos do you want to lead the metrics?
[00:18] Carlos: yeah sure, thanks Maya. so from last run we saw steady state throughput at about 420 requests per second for the small prompt workload, 95th pct latency was around 310 ms when we hit 8 concurrent workers per shard. but during the burst windows we saw queue depth climb and 95th spiked to 740ms. some of that is our batch window configuration and some is concurrency misbalance.
[00:40] Priya: just to confirm — that's with the model pinned to redwood-llama-v2-medium-quant right? the one you shipped for the POC.
[00:50] Carlos: right, redwood-lama-v2-medium-quant — sorry, the transcript may say lama — we used the quantized variant with KV cache enabled. we also had prefix caching for the top 20% repeated requests.
[01:05] Evan: quick question, are those numbers on Dedicated or Hosted? we want to make sure it's apples-to-apples vs our internal infra.
[01:12] Carlos: these were on Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west-2 with 4x A100 equivalent nodes. the dedicated pool was configured with autoscale min=2 max=8 at the time.
[01:23] Liam: and what's the token mix? short prompts or mix? that affects batching obviously.
[01:28] Carlos: good call — the representative workload you gave had 70% short prompts (~50 tokens) and 30% medium prompts (~150 tokens). we also ran a long prompt test but throughput drops as expected.
[01:40] Priya: our SLA target is 95th < 500ms for the short prompt path. we can tolerate up to 1s during long prompt rare cases but main gating metric is short prompt 95th.
[01:50] Maya: okay good, that's achievable. so two levers: continuous batching parameters and concurrency targets. carlos, can you explain how changing the batch_window_ms and max_batch_size shifts the latency/throughput curve?
[02:05] Carlos: sure. short version: increasing batch_window_ms lets the runtime gather more requests into a single kernel run which raises throughput and token efficiency but increases queuing delay for early arrivals. max_batch_size caps GPU utilization — if too small we underutilize, too big and the kernel takes longer and hurts P95 for short tail. for your mix, we found a sweet spot at batch_window_ms=12ms and max_batch_size=128 for the short prompt path. that gave 25% higher throughput and P95 ~ 360ms in steady state.
[02:39] Sanjay: was that with prefix caching on? because we have a lot of repeated prefixes from auth flows.
[02:45] Carlos: yes prefix cache on; that helped reduce compute per request. the spike behavior though looks like during burst the queueing combined with autoscale cooldowns meant we had a delayed scale up.
[02:57] Evan: what's the autoscale cooldown configured at the moment? we want faster reaction to sudden bursts.
[03:02] Maya: currently it's 120s. we recommended 30s for your traffic pattern but didn't push it yet.
[03:08] Priya: 30s sounds reasonable. any downside? more flapping?
[03:12] Anya: might increase churn if you're seeing oscillations; we can add a simple smoothing policy: require 2 consecutive intervals above threshold before scale up, and scale down is more conservative. also add a burst capacity buffer so we don't overshoot.
[03:27] Liam: can we talk about concurrency per model shard? the docs hint at concurrency per GPU and per replica but we need clear targets.
[03:36] Carlos: yes. our runtime supports per-replica concurrency controls; for the A100-equivalent node we recommend 6-10 concurrent requests for the short prompt path depending on quantization. with int8 quant we could push concurrency higher. for you, with the quantized medium, we put target concurrency at 8 and observed best latency/throughput balance.
[03:58] Priya: when you say concurrency = 8, that's simultaneous in-flight requests to the same replica right? not queued on the router.
[04:03] Carlos: correct, that's in-flight. queued requests sit at the router until a slot frees. router queueing policy can be FIFO or priority-based; currently you're on FIFO.
[04:12] Sanjay: the router queue overflow is what caused the 740ms spike?
[04:16] Carlos: mostly — plus autoscale not catching up. some retries from the client exacerbated the queue. we saw retry storms when clients used naive backoff.
[04:26] Priya: oh those retries are from our internal gateway, we can tune backoff to be jittered. good catch.
[04:31] Maya: action item for Priya to change retry to exponential with jitter for the gateway.
[04:36] Priya: noted.
[04:38] Anya: another tuning knob is the queue depth limit per router. if you set a soft limit we can return 429 earlier and let clients backoff instead of letting queue grow. that reduces p95.
[04:49] Evan: would that lose requests? we have some sensitive flows.
[04:52] Carlos: you'd only get rejections when system is under extreme pressure; with proper client backoff, it's better than long tail latencies. also we can use a priority lane for critical reqs — small reserved slot pool.
[05:03] Liam: how about micro-batching vs continuous batching? did you test both?
[05:08] Carlos: yes — micro-batching (fixed periodic batches) was simpler but continuous batching with low-latency window performed better for your traffic. continuous batching adapts when request arrivals are bursty. micro-batching created harsher tail for short prompts.
[05:22] Priya: any changes needed on our side to enable continuous batching?
[05:25] Carlos: none, it's runtime-side. we will share the config flags: batch_window_ms, max_batch_size, batch_alignment and also the sample startup script.
[05:34] Anya: and we'll include the RPC timeouts and recommended client-side concurrency: keep your gateway concurrency at 2x per-replica concurrency to avoid head-of-line blocking.
[05:46] Priya: what's head-of-line blocking in this context?
[05:49] Anya: if the gateway sends a big sequence of requests to a single replica and one takes long (long prompt), it can hold the in-flight slots preventing short prompts from benefiting. spreading across replicas helps.
[05:59] Sanjay: can we route short prompt path to a separate pool? maybe a small low-latency pool optimized for short tokens.
[06:05] Maya: yep, that's a common pattern — route by hint or route key. we can spin up a dedicated low-latency pool with smaller batch_window_ms and lower concurrency. costs a little more but lowers P95 for critical flows.
[06:17] Liam: show me the cost delta, please.
[06:19] Maya: we'll add cost delta to the spreadsheet — rough estimate is +18-25% for a dedicated low-latency pool at your QPS, but it buys consistent P95.
[06:30] Priya: acceptable if it's only for the auth/checkout path.
[06:33] Carlos: next, queueing model — we saw queue depth metrics and spike traces. two observations: many queued batches were dominated by long prompts, so alignment of requests by token length before batching helps; we have a batch_alignment param to prioritize similar sequence lengths. enabling that reduced compute variance and slightly lowered 95th.
[06:55] Evan: interesting — does alignment increase scheduling overhead?
[06:58] Carlos: minimal; it's O(n) bucket sort by length bins before kernel run. tradeoff is slightly higher scheduler CPU but much better GPU kernel efficiency.
[07:10] Priya: can you remind us about KV cache warmup and its effect? our traffic has lots of repeated context for a user session.
[07:18] Carlos: KV cache warms quickly for repeated sessions. warm cache reduces per-token compute and effectively increases throughput. however eviction policy matters: if you have too many distinct sessions per replica, cache hit rate drops. we recommend session affinity at the router for heavy reuse paths.
[07:33] Sanjay: session affinity could cause imbalance — any mitigation?
[07:36] Anya: set affinity ttl short, and autoscale set to keep some slack. also rotate hot sessions across replicas periodically.
[07:46] Liam: ok let's talk about the planned 2-hour load test. what's the exact config you want us to run?
[07:52] Carlos: run the representative mix (70/30 short/medium) at target QPS of 500 sustained with 4x burst to 2000 for 2 minutes every 15 minutes. set gateway concurrency to 16 (we'll recommend final after pilot), enable continuous batching with batch_window_ms=12ms, max_batch_size=128, batch_alignment=enabled, prefix cache on, autoscale cooldown 30s, min replicas 2, max 10. capture p50/p90/p95/p99 and GPU utilization, queue depth, and router rejects.
[08:26] Priya: we'll also capture client-side end-to-end time so we can correlate.
[08:29] Carlos: perfect. and please run with jittered exponential backoff.
[08:33] Maya: any other blockers?
[08:35] Priya: maybe one note — our security team asked about SOC2 controls and audit logs retention for dedicated. Maya can you drop the security pack?
[08:41] Maya: yes I'll send the enterprise security pack, SOC2 attestation, and audit log options. action item for me.
[08:47] Liam: also pricing — after the extended run we need a revised estimate for Dedicated vs mixing hosted + dedicated.
[08:54] Maya: I'll update the pricing worksheet once we have the new numbers; I'll include cost-per-1000-requests and delta for low-latency pool.
[08:59] Priya: one more question — you mentioned retry policies. do you have recommended client SDK defaults?
[09:04] Anya: yes, we recommend per-request timeout = 3s for short prompts, max retries 2, exponential backoff base 200ms with jitter, and global circuit-breaker at gateway after 5 consecutive 5xx. we'll paste the SDK snippet.
[09:18] Sanjay: about monitoring — can we get token-level breakdowns? we want to attribute cost to feature routes.
[09:23] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and per-route latency. we'll enable a demo dashboard and share access.
[09:30] Priya: great.
[09:32] Carlos: recap of technical todos: share continuous-batch config + sample script, share benchmark spreadsheet, recommend final gateway concurrency, and run the 2h load test.
[09:43] Maya: and commercial/security todos: Maya to send security docs and pricing worksheet. Priya to provide request distribution and SLO targets.
[09:52] Priya: we'll aim to run the test Thursday 10am PT and share results by EOD Friday.
[09:58] Maya: perfect — let's pencil in a deep-dive next Wed to go through results. Carlos will lead.
[10:06] Liam: ok thanks everyone. small note — please put the sample config in the repo link you shared earlier (link: https://redwood.ai/poc-configs) so our infra team can pull it.
[10:20] Maya: will do. thanks all.

End of call.

Artifacts referenced: continuous-batch-config.yaml (link: https://redwood.ai/poc-configs/continuous-batch-config.yaml), benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/poc-results/novapay-benchmarks.xlsx), security pack (link: https://redwood.ai/security/enterprise-pack.pdf)

- Priya to run the 2-hour load test (500 QPS sustained, 4x bursts) and send raw results by 2026-10-02.
